correctness.rationale: For the weighted Bergman domain, exact normalized monomials have norms squared q_α(n)=∫_0^1 t^n[log(e/(1-t))]^αdt, while codomain A² monomial norm squared is 1/(m+1). The coefficient matrix is T_{mn}=1/[(m+n+1)√((m+1)q_α(n))], so ∑_{mn}|T_{mn}|²=∑_n J_n/q_α(n), with J_0=ζ(3) and J_n=∑_{k>=1}1/[k(k+n)²]. Exact partial fractions yield J_n=H_n/n²-(ζ(2)-H_n^(2))/n for n>=1. Uniform Laplace substitution u=n(1-t) shows q_α(n)=(log n)^α/n*(1+O(1/log n)) for α∈[2,3], and fixed-real-α leading asymptotic also holds. Harmonic expansion gives J_n=(log n+γ-1)/n²+O(n^-3), hence J_n/q_α(n)~1/[n(log n)^(α-1)]; sum converges iff α>2, directly constructing unique HS extension. Uniform error bound O(1/[n(log n)^α]) at α∈[2,3] makes the model-series residue exact: (α-2)∑_{n>=3}1/[n(log n)^(1+α-2)]→1. Initial terms and summed errors are uniformly bounded, so the squared HS norm residue equals 1. Fresh independently computed rational partial fractions and finite tails for n=1,2,3,7,20,100 passed, supporting but not proving infinite series and uniformity.

originality.rationale: The mapping threshold and endpoint compactness classification are prior results. Resultary complete published reports give compactness for α>2, essential norm 2 at α=2, and an HS perturbation of a normalized endpoint Copson model; none implies the original Hilbert matrix is in S2 for every α>2 or gives its trace and unit pole. Norrbo primary paper is most relevant to the mapping threshold but only its bibliographic/abstract material was accessible in this run; the full article was blocked by disconnected institutional VPN. The sharp trace and residue are thus original on a documented best-of-knowledge basis, with a real risk from general operator ideal theorems.
